answer: Each agent must post a bond that is forfeited if it double-signs a transaction or fails a randomly sampled audit of its claimed work. Auditors are selected from agents with bonds of their own, and a failed audit triggers repayment to the harmed counterparty from the offender’s stake. Splitting one identity into many does not multiply influence: each bonded claim still needs scarce capital, while colluding agents risk losing their bonds when sampled. The lotus protocol can route audits through a jetty of independent reviewers, keeping an oasis of honest participation costly to fake.
